blocks.text: Managers, head coaches and caretaker spells: explore the people who have led Albion, with sources and the matches behind their stories.

blocks.heading: Three profiles to start the story

parts.text: Steve Clarke, Darren Moore and Tony Mowbray begin this collection. Their careers let us explore a single appointment, a caretaker becoming permanent head coach, and a manager returning for a second spell. Earlier managers and other modern appointments are still to be researched.
Birmingham-born Moore was a centre-back and Jamaica international. He joined Albion in September 2001 and helped win promotions in 2002 and 2004, before playing his part in the 2005 Great Escape.
From Saltcoats in Ayrshire, Clarke played for St Mirren and Chelsea before a coaching career that included Chelsea and West Ham.
Mowbray led Albion to the 2007/08 Championship title. His first spell began with a 3–0 home win over Wolves in October 2006 and ended with a goalless draw at Blackburn in May 2009.

An appointment announcement does not always identify the first match in charge. We keep those dates separate, preserve caretaker roles, and flag results that have not yet been reconciled. Statistics belong to their recorded competition and period; a larger total is not necessarily a better comparison.
